changes._why: CreditLimit is nullable (no limit), and <> is unknown against a NULL, so a limit set or removed since the moment was missed; Claude's INTERSECT test, which takes two NULLs as equal
request: Accounts receivable wants the customers whose credit limit is not what it was at a past moment, a limit set or removed since then included, with the limit then and now.
`NOT EXISTS (SELECT then INTERSECT SELECT now)` compares the two with NULLs as equal, which `<>` does not.
changes.sql:
DECLARE @asOf datetime2 = '2015-01-01';
SELECT c.CustomerID, c.CustomerName, h.CreditLimit AS CreditLimitThen, c.CreditLimit AS CreditLimitNow
FROM Sales.Customers c
         JOIN Sales.Customers FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF @asOf h ON h.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT h.CreditLimit
                  INTERSECT
                  SELECT c.CreditLimit)
ORDER BY c.CustomerID

changes._why: FOR SYSTEM_TIME FROM ... TO also returned the reading recorded before @from that was still current at @from; the reading's own time is RecordedWhen
request: Quality control checks the cold rooms over a period: for each sensor, the number of readings recorded in the period and the lowest, highest and average temperature.

Each reading is a version of a row of a system-versioned table, so the query reads them all with `FOR SYSTEM_TIME ALL` and keeps those recorded in the period by `RecordedWhen`; `FROM ... TO` would also return the reading still in force when the period began. This is SQL only.
changes.sql:
DECLARE @from datetime2 = '2016-05-01', @to datetime2 = '2016-05-02';
SELECT ColdRoomSensorNumber,
       COUNT(*)                                 AS Readings,
       MIN(Temperature)                         AS Lowest,
       MAX(Temperature)                         AS Highest,
       CAST(AVG(Temperature) AS decimal(10, 2)) AS Average
FROM Warehouse.ColdRoomTemperatures FOR SYSTEM_TIME ALL
WHERE RecordedWhen >= @from
  AND RecordedWhen < @to
GROUP BY ColdRoomSensorNumber
ORDER BY ColdRoomSensorNumber

changes._why: a customer gets a new version whenever any column changes, so 'every version' listed many where the limit did not
request: Accounts receivable wants the history of a customer's credit limit: each limit it has had, from when it was set, the oldest first.
`FOR SYSTEM_TIME ALL` reads the current row and the history together, and `LAG` keeps the versions whose limit changed, NULLs compared as equal; this is SQL only.
changes.sql:
DECLARE @customerId int = 890;
WITH versions AS (SELECT CustomerID,
                         CreditLimit,
                         ValidFrom,
                         LAG(CreditLimit) OVER (ORDER BY ValidFrom) AS PreviousLimit,
                         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ValidFrom)     AS Version
                  FROM Sales.Customers FOR SYSTEM_TIME ALL
                  WHERE CustomerID = @customerId)
SELECT CustomerID, CreditLimit, ValidFrom AS SetFrom
FROM versions
WHERE Version = 1
   OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT CreditLimit
                  INTERSECT
                  SELECT PreviousLimit)
ORDER BY ValidFrom

changes._why: TOP (5) by revenue alone was unstable at a tie
request: The sales manager wants the five stock items which earned the most in a year, by the invoiced extended price, with the quantity sold; `StockItemID` breaks a tie.
changes.sql:
DECLARE @from date = '2015-01-01', @to date = '2016-01-01';
SELECT TOP (5) si.StockItemID, si.StockItemName, SUM(il.Quantity) AS Quantity, SUM(il.ExtendedPrice) AS Revenue
FROM Sales.InvoiceLines il
         JOIN Sales.Invoices i ON i.InvoiceID = il.InvoiceID
         JOIN Warehouse.StockItems si ON si.StockItemID = il.StockItemID
WHERE i.InvoiceDate >= @from
  AND i.InvoiceDate < @to
GROUP BY si.StockItemID, si.StockItemName
ORDER BY Revenue DESC, si.StockItemID

changes._why: RANK gives a tie one place and can return more than three; the order within a place was undefined
request: The sales manager ranks the salespeople of each year by the invoiced extended price and wants the top three places of each year, all of those tied for a place included, ordered by `PersonID` within a place.
`RANK() OVER (...)`, a window function, is SQL only; a tie for third can return more than three rows.
changes.sql:
WITH yearly AS (SELECT YEAR(i.InvoiceDate) AS SalesYear, i.SalespersonPersonID, SUM(il.ExtendedPrice) AS Revenue
                FROM Sales.Invoices i
                         JOIN Sales.InvoiceLines il ON il.InvoiceID = i.InvoiceID
                GROUP BY YEAR(i.InvoiceDate), i.SalespersonPersonID),
     ranked AS (SELECT y.*, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY y.SalesYear ORDER BY y.Revenue DESC) AS SalesRank
                FROM yearly y)
SELECT r.SalesYear, r.SalesRank, p.PersonID, p.FullName, r.Revenue
FROM ranked r
         JOIN Application.People p ON p.PersonID = r.SalespersonPersonID
WHERE r.SalesRank <= 3
ORDER BY r.SalesYear, r.SalesRank, p.PersonID

changes._why: ORDER BY Outstanding alone left suppliers of one balance in any order; SupplierName is unique
request: Accounts payable wants what is still owed to each supplier: the transactions not finalized, their number and the outstanding balance, the largest first, a tie by name.
`IsFinalized` is a computed column.

FROM Purchasing.SupplierTransactions st
         JOIN Purchasing.Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = st.SupplierID

changes._why: few countries, so equal counts are likely and were in no order; an item without the key forms a NULL group the request did not name
request: Compliance counts the stock items by country of manufacture, which is in the CustomFields JSON document, the most first, a tie by country; the items with no country recorded count as one group.
`JSON_VALUE` is SQL only.

GROUP BY JSON_VALUE(CustomFields, '$.CountryOfManufacture')

changes._why: filtering on InvoiceDate took in unconfirmed deliveries and left out older invoices delivered after the date; the delivery's own time is ConfirmedDeliveryTime
request: Show a customer's deliveries confirmed on or after a date, with the invoice, the confirmation time and who received it, the earliest confirmation first.

changes._why: a city with no location gives a NULL distance, and equal distances made TOP unstable
request: Find the five other cities nearest to a given city, with their state code and the distance in kilometres; a city whose distance cannot be computed is left out, and `CityID` breaks a tie.
changes.sql:
DECLARE @cityId int = 30378; -- San Francisco
SELECT TOP (5) c.CityID, c.CityName, sp.StateProvinceCode, CAST(c.Location.STDistance(o.Location) / 1000 AS decimal(10, 1)) AS Kilometres
FROM Application.Cities c
         JOIN Application.StateProvinces sp ON sp.StateProvinceID = c.StateProvinceID
         JOIN Application.Cities o ON o.CityID = @cityId
WHERE c.CityID <> o.CityID
  AND c.Location.STDistance(o.Location) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY c.Location.STDistance(o.Location), c.CityID

changes._why: equal amounts were in no order; SupplierID breaks the tie
changes.sql:
DECLARE @from date = '2015-01-01', @to date = '2016-01-01';
SELECT s.SupplierName,
       COUNT(DISTINCT po.PurchaseOrderID)                     AS Orders,
       SUM(pol.OrderedOuters * pol.ExpectedUnitPricePerOuter) AS Amount

changes._why: Purchasing has no Advanced exercise, and the nullable delivery dates of purchase orders are used by none
changes.title: The suppliers' late deliveries
request: The buyer rates the suppliers on delivery: for each supplier, the finalized purchase orders received in full, how many of them arrived after the expected delivery date, and the average days late; the most late orders first, a tie by name.
changes.sql:
WITH received AS (SELECT po.PurchaseOrderID, po.SupplierID, po.ExpectedDeliveryDate, MAX(pol.LastReceiptDate) AS ReceivedDate
                  FROM Purchasing.PurchaseOrders po
                           JOIN Purchasing.PurchaseOrderLines pol ON pol.PurchaseOrderID = po.PurchaseOrderID
                  WHERE po.IsOrderFinalized = 1
                    AND po.ExpectedDeliveryDate IS NOT NULL
                  GROUP BY po.PurchaseOrderID, po.SupplierID, po.ExpectedDeliveryDate
                  HAVING COUNT(pol.LastReceiptDate) = COUNT(*))
SELECT s.SupplierName,
       COUNT(*)                                                                                AS Orders,
       SUM(CASE WHEN r.ReceivedDate > r.ExpectedDeliveryDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                AS Late,
       CAST(AVG(CAST(DATEDIFF(day, r.ExpectedDeliveryDate, r.ReceivedDate) AS decimal(10, 1))) AS decimal(10, 1)) AS AverageDaysLate
FROM received r
         JOIN Purchasing.Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = r.SupplierID
GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.SupplierName
ORDER BY Late DESC, s.SupplierName

changes._why: the open orders past their expected date, ranked per supplier
changes.title: Each supplier's three most overdue purchase orders
request: For each supplier, up to three purchase orders not finalized whose expected delivery date is before a cutoff and which have a line not finalized and short-received, the earliest expected first; `PurchaseOrderID` breaks a tie.
changes.sql:
DECLARE @asOf date = '2016-06-01';
WITH overdue AS (SELECT po.PurchaseOrderID,
                        po.SupplierID,
                        po.ExpectedDeliveryDate,
                        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY po.SupplierID ORDER BY po.ExpectedDeliveryDate, po.PurchaseOrderID) AS Position
                 FROM Purchasing.PurchaseOrders po
                 WHERE po.IsOrderFinalized = 0
                   AND po.ExpectedDeliveryDate < @asOf
                   AND EXISTS (SELECT 1
                               FROM Purchasing.PurchaseOrderLines pol
                               WHERE pol.PurchaseOrderID = po.PurchaseOrderID
                                 AND pol.IsOrderLineFinalized = 0
                                 AND pol.ReceivedOuters < pol.OrderedOuters))
SELECT s.SupplierID, s.SupplierName, o.PurchaseOrderID, o.ExpectedDeliveryDate
FROM overdue o
         JOIN Purchasing.Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = o.SupplierID
WHERE o.Position <= 3
ORDER BY s.SupplierName, o.Position

changes._why: Sales.SpecialDeals and its five nullable foreign keys are used by no exercise
changes.title: The special deals in force on a date
request: The sales desk wants the special deals in force on a date: each deal, what it applies to (stock item or stock group, customer, buying group or customer category) and its discount or price, by deal.
changes.sql:
DECLARE @on date = '2016-01-01';
SELECT d.SpecialDealID, d.DealDescription, d.StartDate, d.EndDate,
       si.StockItemName, sg.StockGroupName, c.CustomerName, bg.BuyingGroupName, cc.CustomerCategoryName,
       d.DiscountAmount, d.DiscountPercentage, d.UnitPrice
FROM Sales.SpecialDeals d
         LEFT JOIN Warehouse.StockItems si ON si.StockItemID = d.StockItemID
         LEFT JOIN Warehouse.StockGroups sg ON sg.StockGroupID = d.StockGroupID
         LEFT JOIN Sales.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = d.CustomerID
         LEFT JOIN Sales.BuyingGroups bg ON bg.BuyingGroupID = d.BuyingGroupID
         LEFT JOIN Sales.CustomerCategories cc ON cc.CustomerCategoryID = d.CustomerCategoryID
WHERE d.StartDate <= @on
  AND d.EndDate >= @on
ORDER BY d.SpecialDealID

changes._why: the deals that apply to one customer and item: a NULL key matches anything
changes.title: The special deals that apply to a customer and an item
request: List the special deals that apply to a given customer and stock item on a date, a NULL target meaning no restriction and both dates included, with their three pricing options, without choosing one deal over another.
changes.sql:
DECLARE @customerId int = 1, @stockItemId int = 1, @on date = '2016-05-01';
SELECT sd.SpecialDealID, sd.DealDescription, sd.StartDate, sd.EndDate, sd.DiscountAmount, sd.DiscountPercentage, sd.UnitPrice
FROM Sales.SpecialDeals sd
         JOIN Sales.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = @customerId
         JOIN Warehouse.StockItems si ON si.StockItemID = @stockItemId
WHERE sd.StartDate <= @on
  AND sd.EndDate >= @on
  AND (sd.CustomerID IS NULL OR sd.CustomerID = c.CustomerID)
  AND (sd.BuyingGroupID IS NULL OR sd.BuyingGroupID = c.BuyingGroupID)
  AND (sd.CustomerCategoryID IS NULL OR sd.CustomerCategoryID = c.CustomerCategoryID)
  AND (sd.StockItemID IS NULL OR sd.StockItemID = si.StockItemID)
  AND (sd.StockGroupID IS NULL
    OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Warehouse.StockItemStockGroups sisg WHERE sisg.StockItemID = si.StockItemID AND sisg.StockGroupID = sd.StockGroupID))
ORDER BY sd.SpecialDealID

changes._why: Sales.CustomerTransactions and the credit limit are never compared; a NULL limit is no limit
changes.title: The ten customers using the most of their credit limit
request: Accounts receivable wants the ten customers with a credit limit whose outstanding balance uses the most of it: the limit, the balance of the transactions not finalized, and the share of the limit used; `CustomerID` breaks a tie.
changes.sql:
SELECT TOP (10) c.CustomerID,
                c.CustomerName,
                c.CreditLimit,
                SUM(ct.OutstandingBalance)                                               AS Outstanding,
                CAST(SUM(ct.OutstandingBalance) * 100 / c.CreditLimit AS decimal(10, 1)) AS PercentUsed
FROM Sales.CustomerTransactions ct
         JOIN Sales.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = ct.CustomerID
WHERE ct.IsFinalized = 0
  AND c.CreditLimit > 0
GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CustomerName, c.CreditLimit
ORDER BY PercentUsed DESC, c.CustomerID

changes._why: the stock ledger and TransactionTypes are not used anywhere
changes.title: The movements of a stock item in a year, by transaction type
request: The warehouse manager wants the movements of a stock item in a year: for each transaction type, the number of transactions and the net quantity, by type name.
changes.sql:
DECLARE @stockItemId int = 1, @from datetime2 = '2015-01-01', @to datetime2 = '2016-01-01';
SELECT tt.TransactionTypeName, COUNT(*) AS Transactions, SUM(sit.Quantity) AS Quantity
FROM Warehouse.StockItemTransactions sit
         JOIN Application.TransactionTypes tt ON tt.TransactionTypeID = sit.TransactionTypeID

  AND sit.TransactionOccurredWhen >= @from
  AND sit.TransactionOccurredWhen < @to

changes._why: the ledger's sign convention, in positive, out negative, with conditional sums
changes.title: Incoming and outgoing stock movements
request: For each stock item with movements in a period, the quantity in, the quantity out as a positive amount, and the net movement, by item name.
changes.sql:
DECLARE @from datetime2 = '2016-05-01', @to datetime2 = '2016-06-01';
SELECT si.StockItemID,
       si.StockItemName,
       SUM(CASE WHEN st.Quantity > 0 THEN st.Quantity ELSE 0 END)  AS Incoming,
       SUM(CASE WHEN st.Quantity < 0 THEN -st.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS Outgoing,
       SUM(st.Quantity)                                             AS NetMovement
FROM Warehouse.StockItemTransactions st
         JOIN Warehouse.StockItems si ON si.StockItemID = st.StockItemID
WHERE st.TransactionOccurredWhen >= @from
  AND st.TransactionOccurredWhen < @to
GROUP BY si.StockItemID, si.StockItemName
ORDER BY si.StockItemName
